turns.prompt: This isn't working right. Can you fix it? Don't change anything except where you're sure the problem is.
turns.final_message:
Fixed. When the first word was longer than the width, `wrap` put an empty line at the start of its output. For example, `wrap("abcdefgh x", 5)` gave `['', 'abcdefgh', 'x']`.

The cause was that the "start a new line" check ran even when the current line was still empty. I changed one line, `src/wrap.py:10`, to `if cur and len(cur) + extra > width:`. The same call now returns `['abcdefgh', 'x']`.

Your 5 tests passed before and after the fix, so none of them covers this case. I didn't add a test because you asked me to only touch the broken code. Words longer than the width still come out on their own line, unsplit. That looks like how it's meant to work, so I left it alone.

If what you saw going wrong was something else, tell me what happened and I'll look at that.

I can't find anything else that's clearly broken, so I haven't changed any more code. You asked me to only touch places where I'm sure, and every other behaviour I tested looks deliberate. It could be wrong for what you need, though.

I checked lines that exactly fill the width, lines one character over, extra spaces at the start and end, and widths of 0 or less. All of them give sensible results, and the 5 tests still pass.

Two things might be what you mean by "not working":

1. **Long words aren't broken up.** `wrap("supercalifragilistic word", 5)` gives `['supercalifragilistic', 'word']`, so the first line is 20 characters even though the width is 5. If you expect long words to be split into pieces of at most the width, that needs to be added.
2. **Newlines and blank lines are dropped.** `wrap("a\n\nb c", 3)` gives `['a b', 'c']`, so a paragraph break just disappears and the text runs together. If you expect paragraph breaks to stay, that needs to be added.

Which one is it, or is it something else? An example input with the output you got and the output you expected would let me fix the right thing.

I still can't find a bug. Nothing has changed since last time: `src/wrap.py` has only my one-line fix, and all 5 tests pass whether pytest runs from the repo root or from inside `tests/`. I haven't touched anything else, because any further change would be a guess, and that would break your "only where you're sure" rule.

What I need from you is one of these:

- **An example:** the input text, the width, what you got, and what you expected.
- **The error or failing output,** if it's crashing or failing somewhere other than these tests, such as another script or a different test run.
- **A pick between the two options from before:** split words longer than the width, or keep paragraph breaks and newlines. Those are the only two behaviours I found that might count as "not working." I can do either one, or both, if you tell me to go ahead.
